message.content:
You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`; no internet), the repo layout, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: `|icon|`, `|sign|` and `|image|` — byte-identical to the original.
1. Icons are built-in Phosphor-style symbols (256×256 artwork). Output observed for `|icon| { symbol: house }`: `<g class="lini-node lini-icon" transform="translate(0,0)">` containing `<g transform="scale(0.125) translate(-128 -128)">` (scale = size/256), then `<g fill="var(--lini-icon-fill)" stroke="none"><path d="…"/></g>` (the duotone body) and `<g fill="none" stroke="var(--lini-stroke)" stroke-width="16" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="…"/></g>` (stroke-width counter-scaled = sw/scale, 4 decimals). Fill/stroke come from the node's resolved fill/stroke (palette vars → var(--lini-…)). Unknown symbol → `error: unknown icon 'hous'; did you mean 'house', 'bus', 'horse'?` (find the exact suggestion rule) or `unknown icon 'x'`. The symbol can be given by the label (`|icon| "bell"`) and then extra `[ "3" ]` text rides as a badge-like label — see assets spec_06/spec_08 and icons.lini. You must build the icon data table: discover the full set of valid symbol names (use the "did you mean" suggestions and large candidate word lists — Phosphor has ~1500 names like airplane, alarm, anchor, android-logo, aperture, archive, arrow-*, at, atom, bag, bank, barcode, battery-*, bell, bicycle, book, bookmark, briefcase, browser, bug, building, calendar, camera, car, chart-bar, chat, check, circle, clock, cloud, code, coffee, compass, cpu, credit-card, cube, database, desktop, device-mobile, envelope, eye, file, flag, folder, gear, ghost, globe, hard-drive, heart, house, image, key, laptop, lightning, link, lock, magnifying-glass, map-pin, microphone, moon, music-note, package, paper-plane, pencil, phone, planet, plug, presentation, printer, puzzle-piece, question, rocket, seal, shield, shopping-cart, star, sun, tag, terminal, trash, tree, truck, user, users, video-camera, wall, wallet, warning, warning-circle, wifi, wrench, x… plus weights/variants). For every valid name, extract its body and line path data by compiling it and store the table as data in the repo (e.g. a compact text file under data/ loaded with include_str!). Note the body path may differ from the line path for some icons. `|sign|` is the larger preset (64×64, padding 4, fit: contain|auto, label text inside/under, wireable); work out fit: auto vs contain sizing and label placement from icons.lini and hero.lini.
2. `|image|`: `src:` local file read relative to the input file's directory, embedded as `data:image/png;base64,…` (also check svg/jpg/gif/webp mime types and what an SVG file embeds as), requires width & height (`'|image|' requires 'width' and 'height'`), `fit: auto|contain|cover|stretch` (`preserveAspectRatio` attributes; error text "'fit' must be auto, contain, cover, or stretch"), missing file → `error: cannot read image 'x' — no such file` (span at the src declaration), `--no-fs` behaviour, label handling, CSS (no `.lini-image` rule was observed). Test image: /workspace/assets/test_images/mark.png (8×8 PNG); write test .lini files next to copies of it in /tmp/<you>/.
Hooks: icons/images are primitives Prim::Icon / Prim::Image (types.rs); add rendering in a new module (e.g. src/icon.rs) called from `render::shape_lines`/`render_node`, measuring in layout.rs as needed. Keep shared edits minimal.

Test files: test_doc_examples spec_06, spec_08, prop_src, prop_fit (error cases), blocks equivalents; test_samples icons.lini, hero.lini, shapes.lini (icon tile) — links in those files are someone else's job, get the icon/sign/image parts exact. Before committing, run the full asset comparison (`cmpw.py /tmp/bin-icon/executable assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini assets/test_samples/*.lini`) and ensure nothing regresses (starting count: 71/209). Commit on your branch and report pass counts, the number of icons captured, shared-file edits and gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules

systemPrompt:
You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. - Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. content.content:
From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE).

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# exact SVG path bbox (python port for exploration)
import math, re

def tokenize(d):
    return re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]|[-+]?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?', d)

def arc_center(x1, y1, rx, ry, phi, fa, fs, x2, y2):
    rx, ry = abs(rx), abs(ry)
    cp, sp = math.cos(math.radians(phi)), math.sin(math.radians(phi))
    dx, dy = (x1 - x2) / 2, (y1 - y2) / 2
    x1p = cp * dx + sp * dy
    y1p = -sp * dx + cp * dy
    lam = x1p**2 / rx**2 + y1p**2 / ry**2
    if lam > 1:
        rx *= math.sqrt(lam); ry *= math.sqrt(lam)
    num = rx*rx*ry*ry - rx*rx*y1p*y1p - ry*ry*x1p*x1p
    den = rx*rx*y1p*y1p + ry*ry*x1p*x1p
    co = math.sqrt(max(0, num / den)) if den else 0
    if fa == fs: co = -co
    cxp = co * rx * y1p / ry
    cyp = -co * ry * x1p / rx
    cx = cp * cxp - sp * cyp + (x1 + x2) / 2
    cy = sp * cxp + cp * cyp + (y1 + y2) / 2
    def ang(ux, uy, vx, vy):
        d = (ux*vx + uy*vy) / (math.hypot(ux, uy) * math.hypot(vx, vy))
        a = math.acos(max(-1, min(1, d)))
        return -a if ux*vy - uy*vx < 0 else a
    th1 = ang(1, 0, (x1p - cxp) / rx, (y1p - cyp) / ry)
    dth = ang((x1p - cxp) / rx, (y1p - cyp) / ry, (-x1p - cxp) / rx, (-y1p - cyp) / ry)
    if not fs and dth > 0: dth -= 2 * math.pi
    elif fs and dth < 0: dth += 2 * math.pi
    return cx, cy, rx, ry, th1, dth

def segments(d):
    """yield ('L', p0, p1) / ('C', p0, c1, c2, p1) / ('Q', ...) / ('A', p0, params, p1)"""
    t = tokenize(d)
    i = 0; cmd = 'M'
    cx = cy = sx = sy = 0.0
    lc = None; lq = None
    out = []
    def num():
        nonlocal i
        v = float(t[i]); i += 1; return v
    while i < len(t):
        if t[i].isalpha():
            cmd = t[i]; i += 1
            if cmd in 'Zz':
                out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (sx, sy)))
                cx, cy = sx, sy; lc = lq = None
                continue
        if i >= len(t): break
        rel = cmd.islower()
        ox, oy = (cx, cy) if rel else (0, 0)
        U = cmd.upper()
        if U == 'M':
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            cx, cy, sx, sy = x, y, x, y
            out.append(('M', (x, y)))
            cmd = 'l' if rel else 'L'; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'L':
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (x, y))); cx, cy = x, y; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'H':
            x = num() + ox
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (x, cy))); cx = x; lc = lq = None
        elif U == 'V':
            y = num() + oy
            out.append(('L', (cx, cy), (cx, y))); cy = y; lc = lq = None
        elif U in 'CS':
            if U == 'C':
                x1 = num() + ox; y1 = num() + oy
            else:
                x1, y1 = (2*cx - lc[0], 2*cy - lc[1]) if lc else (cx, cy)
            x2 = num() + ox; y2 = num() + oy
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('C', (cx, cy), (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x, y)))
            lc = (x2, y2); lq = None; cx, cy = x, y
        elif U in 'QT':
            if U == 'Q':
                x1 = num() + ox; y1 = num() + oy
            else:
                x1, y1 = (2*cx - lq[0], 2*cy - lq[1]) if lq else (cx, cy)
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('Q', (cx, cy), (x1, y1), (x, y)))
            lq = (x1, y1); lc = None; cx, cy = x, y
        elif U == 'A':
            rx = num(); ry = num(); rot = num(); fa = num(); fs = num()
            x = num() + ox; y = num() + oy
            out.append(('A', (cx, cy), (rx, ry, rot, fa != 0, fs != 0), (x, y)))
            cx, cy = x, y; lc = lq = None
    return out

content.text:
`|icon|`, `|sign|` and `|image|` now match the original byte-for-byte in every case I tested; the only mismatches left come from links and other features outside this task. Committed on `worktree-agent-ac8377c749be8d2b5` as `b884ef9` and `aa1edeb`.

**Pass counts**
- Full asset comparison: 76/209 (up from 71), with no regressions. The five new passes are spec_06, spec_08, prop_src, prop_fit and drawing_sheet (the last three are the "no such file" error cases).
- blocks/: 6/37 (up from 4; spec_006 and spec_008 now pass).
- icons.lini, hero.lini, shapes.lini, mindmap.lini, sequence.lini, skill_04 and spec_55 still fail as whole files, but every icon/sign node in them is identical to the original. The rest of each file fails on links, gradients, tables or mindmap/sequence layout.
- I built test files with all 1512 icons in 15 fit/size/stroke combinations: all identical, including layout and viewBox. 8,000 random misspellings gave identical "did you mean" messages. Of roughly 250 hand-written icon/image snippets, the only failures are links, gradients and generic validations.

**Icons captured: 1512.** I seeded the list from Phosphor names and checked them against the original. I then probed every name's one-edit neighbourhood (1.3M probes) and found nothing new. The table is in `data/icons.txt` (549 KB), loaded with `include_str!`. Each entry has the body, line and dot elements, the centring offset and the exact artwork bounding box. I recovered the box sizes to full precision because rounding them broke a few stroke widths.

**Behaviour worth knowing**
- Suggestions: names within 2 edits, closest first, then alphabetical, at most 3.
- A label names the symbol; it only clashes with a `symbol:` written directly on the node, not one from a type rule or class.
- `fit`: auto maps the whole 256 canvas; contain and cover fit the artwork's bounding box; stretch scales x and y separately.
- An icon is always square, sized to fit its children (gap 0 by default); `scale` multiplies its width and height.
- Images are recognised by their content, not their extension. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP embed as base64. SVG files are inlined as a nested `<svg>` with their ids renamed. Web and `data:` URLs pass through unchanged.
- An image with no children needs width and height; that error is raised just before layout, after link errors. There is no `.lini-image` CSS rule.

**Shared-file edits (small, additive)**
- `main.rs`: two modules, a validation pass between building the tree and resolving links, and the image size check before layout.
- `scene.rs`: an icon's label is stored on the node.
- `layout.rs`: icons and images use the new measure, and their outer size excludes the stroke.
- `render.rs`: icons and images draw through the shape hook; the `.lini-image` rule is skipped; user rules on `|image|` are written inline.
- `diag.rs`: added the R024 code for the `--no-fs` error.
- `util.rs`: `xml_escape` now turns `'` into `'`. This changes all text output, not just icons: the original escapes apostrophes in text, titles and links, and we didn't.

**Gaps**
- Error order in two rare cases. A bad icon followed by an unknown class gives the class error first (the original reports the icon). The original also reports colour, comma-list and "property has no meaning on this type" errors earlier than we do. Fixing either needs earlier checking passes in shared code.
- Not implemented here because they belong to other areas: gradient fills, "property has no meaning on this type" errors (e.g. `fit` on `|box|`, `multiple` on `|image|`), `--static` colour inlining, the label→`symbol` rewrite in `desugar`, and `scale` for non-icon nodes (I handle it only for icons and images).
- The shadow filter colour ignores `--theme dark`; that is in shared shadow code, not icon-specific.

The discovery and capture scripts are kept outside the repo in `/tmp/icon/disc/`.
